newsitem.title: POLAND: Poles resold 53 pct of mass privatisation units.
newsitem.headline: Poles resold 53 pct of mass privatisation units.

text.p: About 53 percent of Poles who bought mass privatisation units have already sold them on the secondary market, according to a public opinion poll published on Tuesday.
The survey, by the public CBOS agency, showed that out of those who kept the units, 42 percent planned to hold them until they were exchanged into shares of the National Investment Funds (NFI).
Under the mass privatisation programme embracing about 500 small and medium-sized companies, each adult Pole could buy one unit for 20 zlotys ($6.79), in a sale that ended last November.
Nearly 95 percent of the 28 million eligible Poles bought their unit, leading the government to proclaim the scheme a great success in encouraging ordinary people to become shareholders.
Each unit will be exchanged this year into 15 shares, one in each of the 15 NFIs, which will then enter the Warsaw Stock Exchange.
A poll in November, by the private Demoskop agency, showed that less than 50 percent of Poles had resold their units.
The CBOS poll, with a 3.2 percent error margin, was carried out in December 12-17 among a representative group of 1,115 adults.
